prompt: Two angles in a bracket are complementary, and one of them measures $62^\circ$. A classmate says the other one is $118^\circ$. Which response is correct?

choices.label: It is $28^\circ$ — the classmate subtracted from $180^\circ$ instead of $90^\circ$
It is $118^\circ$ — the classmate is right
It is $38^\circ$ — complementary angles add to $100^\circ$
It is $62^\circ$ — complementary angles are always equal

hint: Which total belongs to complementary angles: $90^\circ$ or $180^\circ$?

hints.text: Which total belongs to complementary angles: $90^\circ$ or $180^\circ$?
Complementary means the two add to $90^\circ$, so compute $90 - 62$.

explanation: Complementary angles add to $90^\circ$; supplementary angles add to $180^\circ$.
The classmate computed $180 - 62 = 118$, which would be the SUPPLEMENT, not the complement.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity-check the size
steps: A complement must be smaller than $90^\circ$, since the pair only has $90^\circ$ to share.
An answer of $118^\circ$ is already bigger than the whole budget — that alone flags the mistake. The real answer, $28^\circ$, fits.
